title: WORKPLACE ROMANCE
mv: Abstain from all appearance of evil.
mvp: "Abstain from all appearance of evil.” 1 Thessalonians 5:22
assignment: List five (5) factors that can lead to workplace romance or emotional attachments among colleagues (2x5=10 Marks).

b.x: The workplace is a location where we work to earn a living. This includes shops, offices, factories, stores, or anywhere one goes to earn a livelihood. Workplace romance refers to romantic relationships that develop between co-workers in the workplace. The work environment is a common place where people spend a significant time daily. It is, therefore, necessary to know how to navigate office relationships in a way that honours God, protects personal integrity and respects the workplace.

Many people spend extended hours at work, and frequent interactions can sometimes lead to emotional or physical attachments. While workplace relationships may appear exciting or harmless, Christians who desire to honour God in every area of life must carefully evaluate such relationships in the light of God’s Word (Proverbs 6:27). Joseph’s refusal to compromise with Potiphar’s wife stands as a timeless example of integrity and godliness in the workplace (Genesis 39:7-12).

For those who are married, unchecked closeness or inappropriate friendships with colleagues of the opposite sex can open the door to emotional or physical infidelity. Such relationships can erode marital trust, create divided loyalties between home and work, and weaken one’s spiritual life (Proverbs 6:27-29; 1Corinthians 6:18-20).

Unmarried believers may genuinely meet potential life partners in the workplace; however, caution and self-control are essential. Without clear boundaries, workplace relationships can foster unhealthy attachments that lead to fornication or compromise, distract from academic or career growth, harm personal reputation and Christian testimony, and negatively affect the foundation of future marriages (1Corinthians 10:23; Romans 14:16).

It is also important to recognise that workplace romances—whether involving married or unmarried individuals—can result in gossip, scandal, emotional distress, and even loss of promotion or employment. Such outcomes contradict God’s desire for peace, order, and integrity in our lives (Proverbs 6:16-19).
To avoid getting into messy situations in the workplace, everyone should take note of the following:

i: Avoid secrecy and compromising positions (1 Thessalonians 5:22).
Be accountable to yourself, others and God (Romans 14:12).
Identify your weakness and guard against it.

b.x: The following life lessons will be of great help:

i: A believer’s testimony matters more than pleasure (Ecclesiastes 7:1).
Seek God’s kingdom first in all things (Matthew 6:33).

b.x: Workplace relationships require wisdom, self-control and a commitment to God’s principles (1 Thessalonians 4:3-5).
